guide.name: The Pacific Coast Highway from San Francisco to San Diego
guide.description: Six days down the California coast on CA-1 and US-101, through Big Sur, the Central Coast, Santa Barbara and the Los Angeles beaches to San Diego. Big Sur closes for slides at times; check Caltrans first.

properties.name: Golden Gate Bridge Welcome Center
properties.notes: Start on foot at the south end of the bridge for the classic view back over the bay, then follow CA-1 south through the Presidio and Golden Gate Park to the ocean.

properties.name: Devil's Slide Trail
properties.notes: A 1.3-mile piece of the old cliffside highway, closed to cars when the tunnels opened in 2013 and now a paved path for walkers and cyclists. Small parking lots at each end.
properties.address: Devil's Slide Trail, CA-1, Pacifica, CA 94044

properties.name: Sam's Chowder House
properties.notes: Lobster rolls and chowder at a big roadhouse above the water just north of Half Moon Bay. Ask for the deck when the fog stays offshore.
properties.address: 4210 N Cabrillo Hwy, Half Moon Bay, CA 94019

properties.name: Duarte's Tavern
properties.notes: A family-run tavern in the village of Pescadero since 1894, known for cream of artichoke soup and olallieberry pie. A short detour inland from the coast road.

properties.name: Pigeon Point Light Station State Historic Park
properties.notes: One of the tallest lighthouses on the West Coast. The tower is closed for long-running restoration, but the grounds and cliff overlook are open and good for spotting gray whales in winter and spring.

properties.name: HI Pigeon Point Lighthouse Hostel
properties.notes: Dorm beds and private rooms in the old keepers' houses next to the lighthouse, run by Hostelling International. About the cheapest sea view on the whole trip; check the hostel's site before you go.

properties.name: Año Nuevo State Park
properties.notes: Northern elephant seals breed on these dunes in winter, when access is by guided walk only. The rest of the year a permit hike leads out to the viewing area; check the state park site for reservations.
properties.address: 1 New Years Creek Rd, Pescadero, CA 94060

properties.name: Natural Bridges State Beach
properties.notes: A sea arch, tide pools at the north end, and a eucalyptus grove where monarch butterflies cluster through the late fall and winter.
properties.address: 2531 W Cliff Dr, Santa Cruz, CA 95060

properties.name: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk
properties.notes: A seaside amusement park running since 1907, with the wooden Giant Dipper coaster and a 1911 Looff carousel. Rides run on a reduced schedule outside summer.

properties.name: Dream Inn Santa Cruz
properties.notes: A tall 1960s hotel set right on Cowell Beach, where every room faces the water and the wharf. Walk to the boardwalk in ten minutes.

properties.name: Phil's Fish Market
properties.notes: Cioppino and fried fish in a big, casual seafood hall, now in Castroville after many years at Moss Landing harbor. An easy stop where CA-1 meets the artichoke fields.

properties.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
properties.notes: Built inside an old sardine cannery at the end of Cannery Row, with a three-story kelp forest and a huge open-ocean tank. Book timed tickets ahead in summer and on holidays.

properties.name: Asilomar Hotel & Conference Grounds
properties.notes: Julia Morgan designed the first lodges here a century ago. Rooms are plain, but the dunes boardwalk runs straight to the beach and the price is gentle for this coast.

properties.name: The Lone Cypress
properties.notes: The best-known stop on 17-Mile Drive, the private loop through Pebble Beach that charges a per-car fee at the gates. Bird Rock and Fanshell Overlook along the way are quieter.

properties.name: Carmel Mission Basilica
properties.notes: Mission San Carlos Borromeo, founded in 1771 and the headquarters of the California missions under Junípero Serra. The museum rooms and gardens take about an hour.

properties.name: Cypress Inn
properties.notes: A 1929 Mediterranean-style inn in the middle of the village, once co-owned by Doris Day and still openly welcoming to dogs.

properties.name: La Bicyclette
properties.notes: A small European-style bistro with a wood-fired oven, a short walk from the inns in the village.

properties.name: Point Lobos State Natural Reserve
properties.notes: Granite headlands, cypress groves and coves with harbor seals and sea otters, three miles south of Carmel. Parking inside is limited, so come early.

properties.name: Bixby Creek Bridge
properties.notes: The 1932 concrete arch most people picture when they think of Big Sur. Use the pullout on the north side and keep off the roadway. Highway 1 here closes for slides and storms at times; check Caltrans QuickMap before you set out.

properties.name: Point Sur State Historic Park
properties.notes: An 1889 light station on a volcanic rock above the surf, visited only on guided tours that meet at the gate on Highway 1. Check the state park site for tour days.
properties.address: Point Sur Lighthouse, CA-1, Big Sur, CA 93920

properties.name: Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park
properties.notes: Redwoods along the Big Sur River, a short trail to Pfeiffer Falls and a large campground. Reserve campsites well ahead.

properties.name: Big Sur Lodge
properties.notes: Simple cottages inside the state park, with a restaurant and the river trails at the door. The most affordable roof in Big Sur short of a tent.

properties.name: Glen Oaks Big Sur
properties.notes: A restored 1950s motor lodge plus cabins in the redwoods by the river, with gas fireplaces in most rooms.

properties.name: Big Sur Bakery
properties.notes: Wood-fired bread, pastries and breakfast in a house set back from the highway. A good first stop of the morning.

properties.name: Pfeiffer Beach
properties.notes: Purple-streaked sand and the arch at Keyhole Rock, at the end of a narrow, unsigned road off Highway 1. The lot is small and charges a day-use fee; RVs and trailers can't make the turns.
properties.address: Sycamore Canyon Rd, Big Sur, CA 93920

properties.name: Nepenthe
properties.notes: A family-run terrace restaurant 800 feet above the coast since 1949. Come for a late lunch and the long view south.

properties.name: Post Ranch Inn
properties.notes: The splurge: tree houses and cliff-edge rooms built into the ridge, adults only.

properties.name: McWay Falls
properties.notes: An 80-foot waterfall pouring onto a beach in Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park. The overlook trail from the park lot is short and flat; the beach itself is off limits.
properties.address: Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park, 52801 CA-1, Big Sur, CA 93920

properties.name: Piedras Blancas Elephant Seal Rookery
properties.notes: Thousands of elephant seals haul out on the beach below a free boardwalk, and each season brings something different: births, molting, sparring. Volunteer docents are often on hand.
properties.address: Elephant Seal Vista Point, CA-1, San Simeon, CA 93452

properties.name: Moonstone Beach Boardwalk
properties.notes: A mile-long boardwalk along the bluffs at Cambria's west edge, with sea otters in the kelp and a good spot to watch the sun go down.

properties.name: Cambria Pines Lodge
properties.notes: A rambling lodge in the pines above town, with big gardens, fireplace rooms and live music in the lounge most nights.

properties.name: Linn's Restaurant
properties.notes: Pot pies, comfort plates and olallieberry pie from a family that started with a farm stand outside town.

properties.name: Hearst Castle
properties.notes: William Randolph Hearst's hilltop estate, now a state historic park, ten miles back up the coast from Cambria. All visits are by guided tour from the visitor center; book on the official site, especially in summer.
properties.address: 750 Hearst Castle Rd, San Simeon, CA 93452

properties.name: Morro Rock
properties.notes: A 576-foot volcanic plug at the harbor mouth, protected for nesting peregrine falcons. No climbing; walk the beach on its north side instead.

properties.name: Giovanni's Fish Market & Galley
properties.notes: Fish and chips and clam chowder ordered at the counter and eaten on the waterfront, with sea lions barking from the docks.

properties.name: Mission San Luis Obispo de Tolosa
properties.notes: Founded in 1772, the mission faces a plaza on San Luis Obispo Creek at the edge of downtown. The creekside walk leads to the shops on Higuera Street.
properties.address: 751 Palm St, San Luis Obispo, CA 93401

properties.name: Firestone Grill
properties.notes: A loud, busy downtown spot for the tri-tip sandwich, the Central Coast's signature cut.
properties.address: 1001 Higuera St, San Luis Obispo, CA 93401

properties.name: Madonna Inn
properties.notes: A 1958 roadside hotel where every room has its own theme, plus pink dining rooms and a famous cake case. Stop for a slice even if you are not staying.
properties.address: 100 Madonna Rd, San Luis Obispo, CA 93405

properties.name: Old Mission Santa Barbara
properties.notes: The twin-towered mission above town, with a self-guided tour through the museum, cemetery and gardens. The rose garden across the street is free.

properties.name: Santa Barbara County Courthouse
properties.notes: A 1929 Spanish Colonial Revival courthouse with painted ceilings and tiled stairways. Ride up to the clock tower for the view over the red roofs.

match.skip: Apple Maps only lists a neighboring or larger place here (checked Nov 14, 2026)

properties.name: La Super-Rica Taqueria
properties.notes: A small taqueria with handmade tortillas and a short menu on the wall. Expect a line and a patio seat.
properties.address: 622 N Milpas St, Santa Barbara, CA 93103

properties.name: Hotel Californian
properties.notes: A Moorish-style hotel at the foot of State Street, a block from the beach and close to the Funk Zone's tasting rooms.

properties.name: Neptune's Net
properties.notes: A roadside seafood shack at the county line, where surfers and motorcyclists share picnic tables over fried shrimp and steamed crab.

properties.name: El Matador State Beach
properties.notes: Sea stacks and caves at a small cove below the bluffs, reached by a steep trail and stairs from the lot. Best at low tide.

properties.name: Getty Villa
properties.notes: Greek, Roman and Etruscan antiquities in a re-created Roman country house with gardens above the coast. Admission is free with a timed reservation from the Getty's site.
properties.address: 17985 Pacific Coast Hwy, Pacific Palisades, CA 90272

properties.name: Santa Monica Pier
properties.notes: The 1909 pier with an amusement park, a Ferris wheel over the water and a 1922 carousel. It also marks the western end of Route 66.
properties.address: 200 Santa Monica Pier, Santa Monica, CA 90401

properties.name: Venice Canals
properties.notes: A quiet grid of footpaths and small bridges along the canals Abbot Kinney dug in 1905, two blocks from the noise of the boardwalk.

properties.name: Gjusta
properties.notes: A bakery and deli in a converted warehouse with breads, smoked fish and breakfast plates. Order at the counter and find a seat on the back patio.

properties.name: Hotel Erwin
properties.notes: A mid-range hotel right off the boardwalk, with a rooftop bar that looks over the beach.

properties.name: The Queen Mary
properties.notes: The 1936 ocean liner, moored in Long Beach for good, with original cabins as hotel rooms and decks to explore on a day visit.

properties.name: Crystal Cove State Park
properties.notes: Three miles of beach and tide pools plus a historic district of 1930s beach cottages, some of which rent overnight. Cottage booking opens months ahead; check the official site.
properties.address: 8471 N Coast Hwy, Laguna Beach, CA 92651

properties.name: Beachcomber at Crystal Cove
properties.notes: Breakfast or a sunset drink on a deck right above the sand, in one of the restored cottages of the historic district.

properties.name: Heisler Park
properties.notes: A cliff-top park with gardens, benches and stairways down to small coves and tide pools on Laguna's north end.

properties.name: The Ranch at Laguna Beach
properties.notes: A ranch-style resort in a canyon just across the highway from the beach, with its own nine-hole golf course.

properties.name: Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve
properties.notes: Sandstone bluffs and the rare Torrey pine on short trails above the beach. Park at the beach lot and walk up, or drive to the lodge at the top when spaces allow.
properties.address: 12600 N Torrey Pines Rd, La Jolla, CA 92037

properties.name: La Jolla Cove
properties.notes: A small cove below the village where sea lions and harbor seals sprawl on the rocks. Snorkelers come for the garibaldi in the marine reserve.

properties.name: Point Loma Seafoods
properties.notes: A fish market and counter at the sportfishing docks since 1963. Get a fish sandwich and eat outside watching the boats.

properties.name: Cabrillo National Monument
properties.notes: The tip of Point Loma, with an 1855 lighthouse, views across the bay to downtown, and tide pools on the west side at low tide.
properties.address: 1800 Cabrillo Memorial Dr, San Diego, CA 92106

properties.name: Balboa Park
properties.notes: Spanish Revival buildings from the 1915 exposition, museums, gardens and the botanical building along El Prado. Free to walk around; museums charge separately.

properties.name: Hotel del Coronado
properties.notes: The red-roofed 1888 Victorian resort on Coronado's beach, a fitting last night at the end of the coast road.
